subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Circuit Breakers: Protecting Wires from Fire
description: A 60-second lesson on Circuit Breakers: Protecting Wires from Fire.

hook.text: A 15-amp circuit breaker trips when current exceeds 15 amps. Without it, your walls would catch fire.

buildup.text: Excess current heats wires. If wire insulation melts before anything trips, the exposed metal sparks against wood framing.

discovery.text: Thermal breakers use a bimetallic strip that bends with heat. When current is too high, the strip trips a mechanical switch.

twist.text: Magnetic breakers react in milliseconds to short circuits. Thermal ones handle slow overloads. Modern breakers combine both.

climax.text: Arc-fault breakers detect dangerous arcing — sparks from loose connections. They prevent fires that standard breakers miss.

punchline.text: Too much current? Click. Power off. House saved.

quiz.question: What can arc-fault circuit breakers detect that standard breakers cannot?
options: Water leaks that could cause short circuits in walls
Dangerous sparking from loose connections that could start fires
Voltage spikes from lightning strikes on power lines
